courses.name: Digital Systems I
courses.blurb: How computers work at the lowest level: binary, Boolean algebra, logic gates, combinational and sequential circuits.

comments.title: Why I loved it
comments.text: What I loved about this course was learning how computers work at the lowest level. It was insightful, and it was the beginning of me seeing how everything pieces together when it comes to computers overall.

courses.name: Discrete Mathematics for Computing
courses.blurb: Logic, sets, proofs, counting, recurrences and graphs: the math underneath computer science.

comments.title: So many different topics
comments.text:
The winter is brutal, so I was extra unmotivated to go above and beyond. I had a difficult start, but I ended up performing well in it by the end.

What I loved about discrete math is how diverse the topics are. There are so many different things in it, and that's what makes it so interesting.

documents.note: 13 pages: summary sheets and worked problems. Large file (36 MB), may take a moment to open.

courses.name: Calculus I
courses.blurb: Limits, derivatives and integrals, and all the problems they let you solve.

comments.title: Solving problems in unexpected ways
comments.text:
The winter is brutal, so I was extra unmotivated to go above and beyond. I had a difficult start, but I ended up performing well in it by the end.

What I liked about calculus is how it introduces you to solving all kinds of problems in ways you wouldn't necessarily expect.

courses.name: Introduction to Linear Algebra
courses.blurb: Vectors, lines and planes, subspaces, span, matrices: the language of optimization.

comments.title: The math behind optimization
comments.text:
What I liked is how crucial linear algebra is to optimization systems. It really put into perspective how things can genuinely be specified.

I spent my whole high school career optimizing individual functions one by one because I was so unaware, but now it's very good to know, lol.

courses.name: Spanish
courses.blurb: Grammar, verb conjugation and vocabulary, with a dose of culture.

comments.title: A reintroduction to a language I love
comments.text:
I liked this course because it was a reintroduction to proper grammar and overall knowledge of the language.

I had my first Spanish class when I was 9, and ever since, I've loved the culture, including the language.

documents.title: Spanish notes
documents.note: 4 pages, including midterm summary sheets (14 MB).

courses.name: Introduction to Calculus and Vectors
courses.blurb: Ontario grade 12 math, sped up: functions, limits, derivatives and vectors.

comments.title: My first uni term
comments.text:
Since I decided to skip CEGEP and go directly to university, I had to take this as a makeup class. It's essentially a sped-up course on what you would learn in grade 12 math in Ontario.

I liked this course, but it stressed me out because it was my first university term. I was so proud when I did well in it.

documents.title: Calculus and vectors notes
documents.note: 6 pages, including midterm and final exam summary sheets (22 MB).
